result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and a same-day quiz don't show job impact, and both give the director honest wording. A wins narrowly because it proposes re-testing knowledge 1–2 weeks later with changed scenarios. B's 'retention' item is about staff attrition, not what agents remember. B is stronger on specific timing (30/60/90 days) and on naming confounds, but its plan is somewhat heavier for a team of 12. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that completion, satisfaction and a same-day quiz don't show the program worked, and both give the director usable wording. B is narrowly better: it explicitly re-tests agents after the course, has leads score real tickets, and keeps the plan small by picking one or two metrics and defining success in advance. A gives clearer 30/60/90-day timing and fuller caveats about confounds, but it never re-checks what agents remember later and its metric list runs longer.
